task.title: M1: Plain-text size baseline for files without a grammar
task.description:
Files that no language config handles (index.html, CSS, Markdown, YAML, JSON, SQL, shell scripts, and so on) get no file record at all, so they are invisible in the treemap and compare views even though their size and churn are useful. The design says every language gets a baseline that runs with Node alone, with a plain-text fallback. Add a text adapter that always matches and records a size-only entry for every tracked file not claimed by another language config: lang = the extension without the dot (or 'text' when none), loc = total lines, code = non-blank lines, no comments, no complexity, no functions, no edges. Skip binaries (a NUL byte in the first 8 KB), files over 1 MB, and a short denylist of generated files that would swamp the treemap (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, bun.lock, bun.lockb, pnpm-lock.yaml, go.sum, Cargo.lock, Gemfile.lock, *.min.js, *.min.css, *.map). Do not add these languages to the snapshot's languages tier map; the tier badges stay for grammar-backed languages. The history layer already attaches churn by path, so churn coloring works unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:
- Analyzing workbook yields file records for its .html, .css, .md, .yaml, .sql and shell files with loc and code, and the treemap shows them sized by code lines, grey in complexity mode and colored in churn mode.
- TS and Go files are still analyzed only by their own adapters (no duplicate or overwritten records; the merge must not clobber complexity with the text record).
- Binary files, files over 1 MB, and denylisted files produce no record.
- Compare shows added/removed/modified deltas for these files.
- Capacitor's TS numbers (files=361 with ts lang, 3178 functions, 699 edges) are unchanged, and the total file count grows by the number of other text files.
- One fixture test covers an html, a md, a binary, and a denylisted file in a temp repo.
